thought.text: All 20 containers report healthy. The `event` container is showing a recent uptime, which is different from the others, so I'll check its logs and try probing the actual HTTP endpoint.

reasoning_content:
The reason ss/netstat didn't work is possibly because these tools don't exist in the host container. Instead, I'll check the ports with curl. Also, an interesting point: the "event" container is displayed as "Up About a minute" — this suggests that it was recently restarted (probably by me, or the environment was restarted). Wait — the summary says the event was restarted after recovery. But it's currently showing "Up About a minute" while the others are "Up 5-6 minutes". This is strange. It's possible that the environment restarted, or event crashed and got restarted. I'll check the event's logs and its health status.

I'll try curl-ing the service endpoint.

action.command: for p in 8080 8081 8082 8100 8101 8102 8103 8104 8105 7007; do code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/resp_$p.txt -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 10 http://localhost:$p/ 2>&1); echo "port $p -> HTTP $code ($(wc -c < /tmp/resp_$p.txt 2>/dev/null) bytes)"; done
